admission-controller.md.title: Admission Controller
admission-controller.md.summary: An Admission Controller is a piece of code that intercepts requests to the Kubernetes API server before an object is persisted. These controllers can be validating, mutating, or both, and can reject or modify requests.

admission-policies.md.title: Validating and Mutating Admission Policies
admission-policies.md.summary: This document explains declarative admission policies in Kubernetes, detailing Validating and Mutating policies. It covers the use of Common Expression Language (CEL) for validation and mutation logic.

admission-webhooks-good-practices.md.title: Admission Webhook Good Practices
admission-webhooks-good-practices.md.summary: This document outlines best practices for designing and implementing admission webhooks in Kubernetes. It covers considerations for performance, preventing loops, managing mutations, and ensuring compatibility across API version upgrades.

affinity.md.title: Kubernetes Affinity Rules
affinity.md.summary: This document explains Kubernetes affinity, which are rules used to guide the scheduler on where to place pods. It details the two main types of affinity and how they are defined using labels and selectors.

aggregation-layer.md.title: Aggregation Layer
aggregation-layer.md.summary: The aggregation layer allows users to install additional Kubernetes-style APIs in a cluster. It explains how to add `APIService` objects to claim a URL path in the Kubernetes API.

annotation.md.title: Annotation Metadata
annotation.md.summary: This document explains what an annotation is, defining it as a key-value pair used to attach arbitrary, non-identifying metadata to objects. It details that this metadata can be small, large, structured, or unstructured.

api-group.md.title: Kubernetes API Groups
api-group.md.summary: This document explains what Kubernetes API Groups are, which are sets of related paths in the Kubernetes API. It details how API groups can be used to enable or disable API paths for easier extension.

api-resource.md.title: Kubernetes API Resource Definition
api-resource.md.summary: This document defines what an API resource is within the Kubernetes type system. It explains that a resource corresponds to an endpoint on the Kubernetes API server and defines the schema for objects or operations.

api-server-bypass-risks.md.title: Kubernetes API Server Bypass Risks
api-server-bypass-risks.md.summary: This document describes ways security controls within the Kubernetes API server can be bypassed. It focuses on risks introduced by static pods and direct access to the kubelet API.

app-container.md.title: Application Containers in Pods
app-container.md.summary: This document explains what application containers are within a pod and how they relate to init containers. It clarifies the role of init containers in separating initialization tasks from the main application workload.

application-architect.md.title: Application Architect Role
application-architect.md.summary: This document defines the role of an Application Architect, focusing on high-level application design. It explains how an architect ensures an application's implementation allows for scalable and maintainable interaction with surrounding components.

application-security-checklist.md.title: Application Security Checklist
application-security-checklist.md.summary: This document provides a checklist of basic guidelines for securing applications running in Kubernetes from a developer's perspective. It covers areas like application design, service accounts, and container security contexts.

approver.md.title: Approver Role Definition
approver.md.summary: This document defines the role of an Approver, who reviews and approves Kubernetes code contributions. Approval involves a holistic acceptance covering compatibility, conventions, performance, and system interactions.

architecture.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Architecture
architecture.md.summary: This document outlines the necessary components for a complete Kubernetes cluster, detailing the roles of the control plane and worker nodes. It explains how these components interact to manage workloads and ensure cluster functionality.

authentication-mechanisms.md.title: Hardening Guide - Authentication Mechanisms
authentication-mechanisms.md.summary: This document guides users on selecting and securing appropriate authentication mechanisms for a Kubernetes cluster. It details the pros and cons of various built-in methods to help users choose the best security approach.

authorization.md.title: Kubernetes Authorization Mechanism
authorization.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes authorization works by detailing the process of evaluating API requests against configured policies. It covers request attributes, authorization verdicts, and the role of different authorization modules.

autoscaling.md.title: Autoscaling Workloads
autoscaling.md.summary: This document explains how workloads in Kubernetes can be scaled based on resource demand. It details manual scaling methods and automatic horizontal and vertical scaling techniques.

cadvisor.md.title: cAdvisor Overview
cadvisor.md.summary: cAdvisor is a daemon that provides container users with insights into the resource usage and performance characteristics of running containers. It collects, aggregates, and exports information regarding resource usage and network statistics.

cdi.md.title: Container Device Interface (CDI)
cdi.md.summary: The Container Device Interface (CDI) is a specification defining how devices are configured inside containers. It works with device plugins and Dynamic Resource Allocation to provide workloads with necessary device setups like bind mounts or environment variables.

cel.md.title: Common Expression Language (CEL)
cel.md.summary: CEL is a general-purpose expression language designed to be fast, portable, and safe. It is used in Kubernetes for running queries and performing fine-grained filtering on requests and resources.

certificate.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Certificate
certificate.md.summary: This document explains what a certificate is in the context of a Kubernetes cluster. It details how certificates are used to cryptographically secure access to the Kubernetes API for applications.

cgroup.md.title: cgroup (control group)
cgroup.md.summary: cgroup is a Linux kernel feature that allows for the resource isolation, accounting, and limiting of resource usage for a group of processes. It manages CPU, memory, disk I/O, and network usage.

cidr.md.title: CIDR Notation in Networking
cidr.md.summary: CIDR is a notation used to describe blocks of IP addresses. It is heavily used in networking configurations, particularly in Kubernetes for assigning IP addresses to Nodes and Pods.

cla.md.title: Contributor License Agreement (CLA)
cla.md.summary: This document outlines the terms under which a contributor grants a license to an open-source project for their contributions. CLAs are used to resolve legal disputes regarding contributed material and intellectual property.

cloud-controller-manager.md.title: Cloud Controller Manager
cloud-controller-manager.md.summary: The Cloud Controller Manager is a Kubernetes control plane component that embeds cloud-specific control logic. It links a cluster to a cloud provider's API, separating cloud interaction logic from core Kubernetes cluster interactions.

cloud-native-security.md.title: Cloud Native Security and Kubernetes
cloud-native-security.md.summary: This document explains cloud-native information security principles applied to Kubernetes. It outlines security controls and practices across the development, distribution, and deployment lifecycle phases.

cloud-provider.md.title: Cloud Provider Definition
cloud-provider.md.summary: This document defines what a cloud provider is and explains the different types of cloud services they offer. It distinguishes between IaaS and PaaS offerings.

cluster-administration.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Administration Overview
cluster-administration.md.summary: This document provides an overview for creating and administering Kubernetes clusters. It covers planning, managing, and securing clusters, along with considerations for different deployment environments.

cluster-operations.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Operations
cluster-operations.md.summary: This document outlines the work involved in managing a Kubernetes cluster, covering day-to-day operations and coordinating upgrades. It lists examples of cluster operations such as scaling, upgrades, security implementation, and networking configuration.

cluster-operator.md.title: Cluster Operator Role
cluster-operator.md.summary: This document defines the role of a Cluster Operator, which is responsible for configuring, controlling, and monitoring clusters. It clarifies that this role involves maintaining cluster uptime through maintenance and upgrades.

cluster.md.title: Cluster Definition
cluster.md.summary: This document defines a cluster as a set of worker machines (nodes) that run containerized applications. It explains the roles of worker nodes hosting Pods and the control plane managing the cluster for fault tolerance.

cncf.md.title: Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF)
cncf.md.summary: The CNCF builds ecosystems and a community around projects that orchestrate containers in microservices architectures. Kubernetes is a key project within the CNCF, aiming to make cloud native computing ubiquitous.

cni.md.title: Container Network Interface (CNI)
cni.md.summary: This document introduces Container Network Interface (CNI) plugins, which are network plugins that follow the appc/CNI specification. It provides a foundational explanation of what CNI is within the context of container networking.

components.md.title: Kubernetes Components Overview
components.md.summary: This document provides a high-level overview of the essential components that constitute a Kubernetes cluster. It details the core components, control plane elements, node components, and optional addons.

condition.md.title: Kubernetes Resource Conditions
condition.md.summary: This document explains what a condition is in Kubernetes, which is a field in a resource's status describing its current state. Conditions use a type, status (True, False, or Unknown), and optional fields to communicate resource status.

configuration.md.title: Kubernetes Configuration Mechanisms
configuration.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes separates configuration from code using APIs like ConfigMaps and Secrets. It also details methods for injecting configuration via sidecar or init containers.

container-env-variables.md.title: Container Environment Variables
container-env-variables.md.summary: This document explains what container environment variables are and their purpose within containers running in a pod. They provide necessary information and details about the container and related cluster resources.

container-runtime.md.title: Container Runtime
container-runtime.md.summary: The container runtime is a fundamental component that enables Kubernetes to effectively run containers. It is responsible for managing the execution and lifecycle of containers within the Kubernetes environment.

container.md.title: Container Definition
container.md.summary: This document defines a container as a lightweight, portable executable image containing software and its dependencies. It explains how containers decouple applications from the host infrastructure for easier deployment and scaling.

containerd.md.title: containerd overview
containerd.md.summary: containerd is a container runtime designed for simplicity, robustness, and portability. It functions as a daemon to handle tasks like fetching images, executing containers, and managing network access.

containers.md.title: Containers and Container Images
containers.md.summary: This document explains the concepts of containers, container images, and container runtimes. It details how containers decouple applications from infrastructure and the principles of immutable container images.

contributor.md.title: Contributor Definition
contributor.md.summary: This document defines what a 'Contributor' is within the context of the Kubernetes project. It outlines the types of contributions individuals can make to the project and the ways they can help.

control-plane.md.title: Control Plane
control-plane.md.summary: The Control Plane is the container orchestration layer responsible for exposing APIs and interfaces to define, deploy, and manage the lifecycle of containers. It is composed of various components that manage the orchestration process.

cpu-constraint-namespace.md.title: Configure Minimum and Maximum CPU Constraints for a Namespace
cpu-constraint-namespace.md.summary: This document explains how to set minimum and maximum CPU resource constraints for Pods within a Kubernetes namespace using a LimitRange object. It details the steps to create the LimitRange and how Pods must adhere to these rules.

cpu-default-namespace.md.title: Configure Default CPU Requests and Limits for a Namespace
cpu-default-namespace.md.summary: This document explains how to configure default CPU requests and limits for a Kubernetes namespace using a LimitRange. It details how the control plane applies these defaults when containers do not specify their own resource settings.

cri-o.md.title: CRI-O Overview
cri-o.md.summary: CRI-O is a tool that enables the use of OCI container runtimes with Kubernetes CRI. It allows Kubernetes to utilize any OCI-compliant runtime for running Pods and fetching container images from remote registries.

cron-jobs.md.title: CronJob Documentation
cron-jobs.md.summary: This document explains what a CronJob is, how it creates scheduled jobs, and the syntax used to define their execution schedules. It details the structure of a CronJob specification.

csi.md.title: Container Storage Interface (CSI)
csi.md.summary: The Container Storage Interface (CSI) defines a standard interface for exposing storage systems to containers. It allows vendors to create custom storage plugins for Kubernetes as out-of-tree plugins.

customresourcedefinition.md.title: CustomResourceDefinition (CRD)
customresourcedefinition.md.summary: A CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) is an API object used to define a new custom API on the Kubernetes API server. It allows users to extend the built-in Kubernetes API to meet specific environmental needs.

daemonset.md.title: DaemonSet
daemonset.md.summary: A DaemonSet ensures that a copy of a Pod runs on every (or selected) Node in the cluster. It explains how DaemonSets are used for running node-level services and the structure required to define one.

debug-application.md.title: Troubleshooting Applications
debug-application.md.summary: This document provides resources for fixing issues with containerized applications. It covers common problems with Kubernetes resources, interpreting container termination messages, and debugging running containers.

debug-cluster.md.title: Troubleshooting Clusters
debug-cluster.md.summary: This document provides guidance on troubleshooting Kubernetes clusters, covering how to list nodes, debug down or unreachable nodes, and examine logs for cluster health.

debug.md.title: Monitoring, Logging, and Debugging Guide
debug.md.summary: This guide provides resources for gathering information and resolving issues related to application debugging, cluster troubleshooting, logging, and monitoring within Kubernetes. It directs users to various community forums for further assistance.

deployment.md.title: Kubernetes Deployment Management
deployment.md.summary: This document explains how to use Kubernetes Deployments to manage the desired state of Pods and ReplicaSets. It covers creating, updating, rolling back, scaling, and managing the status of deployments.

device-plugin.md.title: Device Plugin
device-plugin.md.summary: Device plugins run on worker nodes to provide Pods with access to infrastructure resources, like local hardware, that need vendor-specific setup. They advertise these resources to the kubelet so workloads can utilize hardware features.

device-plugins.md.title: Device Plugins
device-plugins.md.summary: This document explains the Kubernetes device plugin framework, allowing vendors to advertise system hardware resources like GPUs or NICs to the kubelet. It details the registration process and how users request these extended resources in Pod specifications.

device.md.title: Definition of a Device
device.md.summary: This document defines what a 'Device' is within the infrastructure context. It explains that devices are infrastructure resources attached to nodes, such as GPUs or custom hardware, which require drivers for Kubernetes Pods to access them.

deviceclass.md.title: DeviceClass
deviceclass.md.summary: A DeviceClass is a category of cluster devices that can be used with dynamic resource allocation. Administrators use DeviceClasses to define sets of devices that can be claimed for workloads.

disruption.md.title: Kubernetes Pod Disruptions
disruption.md.summary: This document defines what a disruption is in Kubernetes, which occurs when one or more Pods go out of service. It distinguishes between voluntary disruptions caused by operator actions and involuntary disruptions caused by node or zone failures.

dns-pod-service.md.title: DNS for Services and Pods
dns-pod-service.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes creates DNS records for Services and Pods to enable service discovery. It details namespace scoping, DNS record types like A/AAAA and SRV records, and how Pods configure their DNS.

docker.md.title: Docker Engine Overview
docker.md.summary: This document explains Docker, a software technology that provides operating-system-level virtualization through containers. It details how Docker uses Linux kernel features like cgroups and namespaces to achieve resource isolation.

dockershim.md.title: Dockershim Component in Kubernetes
dockershim.md.summary: Dockershim is a component in Kubernetes versions up to 1.23 that enabled the kubelet to communicate with the Docker Engine. It has been removed in Kubernetes version 1.24 and later.

downstream.md.title: Downstream (disambiguation)
downstream.md.summary: This document clarifies the usage of the term 'downstream' within the Kubernetes ecosystem and Git. It explains that it refers to code or tools that depend on the core Kubernetes codebase or a forked repository.

downward-api.md.title: Downward API
downward-api.md.summary: The Downward API allows containers to consume information about themselves or the cluster without coupling them to the Kubernetes client. It details the fields available via `fieldRef` and `resourceFieldRef` for exposing Pod and container information.

drain.md.title: kubectl drain command for evicting Pods
drain.md.summary: This document explains the process of safely evicting Pods from a Node to prepare it for maintenance or removal. It details the use of the `kubectl drain` command and its behavior regarding eviction retries.

dual-stack.md.title: IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack
dual-stack.md.summary: This document explains how IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack networking enables the allocation of both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses to Kubernetes Pods and Services. It details the prerequisites, configuration steps, and service options for enabling this feature.

duration.md.title: Kubernetes Duration Format
duration.md.summary: This document explains how duration values are represented in Kubernetes APIs. It details the format using non-negative integers combined with specific time unit suffixes.

dynamic-volume-provisioning.md.title: Dynamic Volume Provisioning
dynamic-volume-provisioning.md.summary: This document explains dynamic volume provisioning, which allows users to request automatic creation of storage volumes. It details how this process eliminates the need for manual storage pre-provisioning.

endpoint-slice.md.title: EndpointSlice Tracking
endpoint-slice.md.summary: EndpointSlices track the IP addresses of backend endpoints, typically associated with a Service and representing Pods. The control plane usually manages these automatically, but manual definition is possible.

endpoint-slices.md.title: EndpointSlices
endpoint-slices.md.summary: This document describes EndpointSlices in Kubernetes, which contain references to network endpoints for a Service. It explains the API, address types, conditions like serving, terminating, and ready, and topology information.

endpoint.md.title: Endpoints API Deprecation
endpoint.md.summary: This document explains the Endpoints API, noting that it is deprecated. Kubernetes now uses EndpointSlices instead of the original Endpoints API due to scalability concerns.

ephemeral-container.md.title: Ephemeral Container
ephemeral-container.md.summary: An ephemeral container is a container type that can be temporarily run inside a pod for diagnostics. They lack resource guarantees and should not be used for running the main workload.

etcd.md.title: etcd
etcd.md.summary: etcd is a consistent and highly-available key-value store that serves as the backing store for all cluster data in Kubernetes. This document introduces etcd and advises on the necessity of having a backup plan for its data.

event.md.title: Kubernetes Event Object
event.md.summary: This document explains what a Kubernetes Event object is, describing it as an object that describes state changes or notable occurrences in the cluster. It advises consumers to treat events as best-effort, supplemental data.

eviction.md.title: Pod Eviction Process
eviction.md.summary: This document explains the process of terminating one or more Pods on Nodes. It distinguishes between two types of eviction: Node-pressure eviction and API-initiated eviction.

extend-kubernetes.md.title: Extending Kubernetes
extend-kubernetes.md.summary: This document describes how to customize a Kubernetes cluster by focusing on extensions rather than simple configuration changes. It introduces extension points and patterns for adapting Kubernetes to specific operational needs.

extensions.md.title: Kubernetes Extensions
extensions.md.summary: Extensions are software components that deeply integrate with Kubernetes to support new types of hardware. Most users benefit from pre-installed extensions in hosted or distribution Kubernetes clusters.

feature-gates.md.title: Feature Gate Control in Kubernetes
feature-gates.md.summary: Feature gates are opaque string values used to control which Kubernetes features are enabled within a cluster. They can be enabled or disabled using the `--feature-gates` command-line flag on Kubernetes components.

finalizer.md.title: Kubernetes Finalizers
finalizer.md.summary: Finalizers are namespaced keys used in Kubernetes to delay the full deletion of resources until specific conditions are met. They allow controllers to perform necessary cleanup actions before the object is permanently removed.

flexvolume.md.title: FlexVolume Deprecation and CSI Driver Recommendation
flexvolume.md.summary: This document describes FlexVolume, a deprecated interface for creating out-of-tree volume plugins in Kubernetes. It explains that the Container Storage Interface (CSI) is the recommended replacement for these functionalities.

gateway.md.title: Gateway API Overview
gateway.md.summary: This document describes the Gateway API, an add-on providing API kinds for dynamic infrastructure provisioning and advanced traffic routing. It outlines the design principles and the core resource model components.

glossary-api-eviction.md.title: API-initiated eviction
glossary-api-eviction.md.summary: This document explains the process of using the Eviction API to create an Eviction object that triggers graceful pod termination. It clarifies how API-initiated evictions interact with PodDisruptionBudgets and termination grace periods.

glossary-configmap.md.title: ConfigMap API Object
glossary-configmap.md.summary: This document describes the ConfigMap API object, which is used to store non-confidential data in key-value pairs. It explains how pods can consume this data as environment variables, command-line arguments, or configuration files.

glossary-container-lifecycle-hooks.md.title: Container Lifecycle Hooks
glossary-container-lifecycle-hooks.md.summary: This document explains container lifecycle hooks, which allow users to execute code at specific points during a container's lifecycle. It details the PostStart and PreStop hooks available for containers.

glossary-controller.md.title: Kubernetes Controllers
glossary-controller.md.summary: Controllers in Kubernetes are control loops that monitor the cluster state and initiate necessary changes to move the current state toward the desired state. They watch the cluster state via the API server and are core to Kubernetes operations.

glossary-cri.md.title: Container Runtime Interface (CRI)
glossary-cri.md.summary: The Container Runtime Interface (CRI) is the main protocol used for communication between the kubelet and the container runtime. It defines the gRPC protocol for this interaction.

glossary-deployment.md.title: API Object for Replicated Applications
glossary-deployment.md.summary: This document describes an API object used to manage replicated applications, which typically run Pods without local state. It explains that each replica is a Pod distributed across cluster nodes.

glossary-downward-api.md.title: Downward API
glossary-downward-api.md.summary: The Downward API is Kubernetes' mechanism for exposing Pod and container field values to code running inside a container. It allows containers to access self-information or cluster context without directly coupling them to the Kubernetes API.

glossary-dra.md.title: Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA)
glossary-dra.md.summary: Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) is a Kubernetes feature that allows for the request and sharing of resources like hardware accelerators among Pods. It works by defining device classes for drivers and admins to claim resources for workloads.

glossary-garbage-collection.md.title: Garbage Collection
glossary-garbage-collection.md.summary: Garbage collection in Kubernetes refers to the mechanisms used to clean up cluster resources. This includes removing unused containers, failed Pods, orphaned objects, completed Jobs, and expired resources.

glossary-kube-scheduler.md.title: kube-scheduler
glossary-kube-scheduler.md.summary: The kube-scheduler is a control plane component responsible for watching for Pods without an assigned node and selecting the appropriate node for them. It considers various factors like resource requirements, constraints, and affinity specifications to make scheduling decisions.

glossary-kubectl.md.title: Kubectl Command Line Tool
glossary-kubectl.md.summary: Kubectl is a command-line tool used to communicate with a Kubernetes cluster's control plane via the Kubernetes API. It allows users to create, inspect, update, and delete Kubernetes objects.

glossary-kubernetes-api.md.title: Kubernetes API
glossary-kubernetes-api.md.summary: This document describes the HTTP API that enables communication between users, cluster components, and external components. It explains how Kubernetes resources are managed through RESTful calls to the API.

glossary-logging.md.title: Logging Overview
glossary-logging.md.summary: This document explains what logs are, defining them as lists of events recorded by a cluster or application. Logs are essential for debugging issues and monitoring cluster activity.

glossary-mixed-version-proxy.md.title: Mixed Version Proxy (MVP)
glossary-mixed-version-proxy.md.summary: This feature allows a kube-apiserver to proxy resource requests to a different peer API server. It enables resource requests to be served by the correct API server when multiple API servers with different Kubernetes versions are running in a cluster.

glossary-node-pressure-eviction.md.title: Node-pressure eviction
glossary-node-pressure-eviction.md.summary: Node-pressure eviction is the kubelet's proactive process to terminate pods on nodes to reclaim resources. It monitors resource consumption (CPU, memory, disk space, inodes) to prevent resource starvation.

glossary-pod-lifecycle.md.title: Pod Lifecycle
glossary-pod-lifecycle.md.summary: This document describes the sequence of states a Pod passes through during its entire lifetime. It defines the five possible phases a Pod can be in.

glossary-pod-security-policy.md.title: Pod Security Policy Deprecation
glossary-pod-security-policy.md.summary: This document explains the Pod Security Policy (PSP), a former Kubernetes API used to enforce security restrictions on pod creation and updates. It notes that PSP has been deprecated and removed in recent Kubernetes versions.

glossary-secret.md.title: Introduction to Secrets
glossary-secret.md.summary: This document explains what Secrets are, detailing that they store sensitive information like passwords and keys. It describes how Secret values are stored and how Pods can reference them.

glossary-security-context.md.title: Security Context Definition
glossary-security-context.md.summary: This document explains the `securityContext` field, which defines privilege and access control settings for a Pod or container. It details how to configure the user, group, and security policies within this context.
